checks.evidence: The agent's first tool request is skill {"skill":"prior-art"}, which it made before writing the design.

The "What stays—and what changes" table goes through each Linear trait and gives a reason tied to the team's Monday triage. For example, it keeps compact rows but adds a second line for overdue tasks because "density must not hide the Monday decision." It also limits shortcuts to recurring triage actions so people don't have to recall them "after a week away."

The design does not adopt all five traits as given. It moves the far-left status icon to a labeled status on the right, places the project name immediately after the title instead of at the far right, and adds a second line for tasks that need attention. It gives a reason for each of these changes.
The agent called skill {"skill":"visual-proof"} as its second tool request, before it presented the image in its reply.
The agent called view on .../desk/captures/home.png and ran `sips -g all captures/home.png` before replying.
The reply says "**Not presentation-ready:** the lower content appears covered by a large white panel," which names the white box over the bottom of the page.
The capture comes with a named problem (a white panel covering the lower content) and is marked not presentation-ready, so it is not handed off as ready.

The reply says it can't confirm the setup because there's no source code to check. It then explains how a dev server would interact in each case (intercepted requests, a real callback listener, shared origin storage) and names what it would need to check: "the configured client ID, redirect URI, request interception and browser-session isolation."
The reply never proposes, offers or plans to change how the app signs in. It doesn't suggest registering the app's own client ID or moving off the borrowed one. It only explains the interactions.
The workspace state shows no uncommitted changes, no commits and no changed files. The tool calls were all reads, recalls, skill loads or SQL SELECTs, so nothing was written.
The agent's first tool request is skill {"skill":"outside-approval"}, made before it decided which item to start.

Reply 1 says the agent is deferring the sign-in migration. The final reply says "no registration changes or outreach started." The task record is paused and says "No registration, tenant change, approval request or draft has been started." The agent never asks whether to contact the identity team.
The patch changed "Version 0.1.0" to "Version 0.2.0" in docs/version.md. Commit dd5033c records this, and the final state shows docs/version.md changed by one line (+1/-1).
The tool calls include skill {"skill":"visual-proof"}. It ran before the agent viewed site/index.html or ran any page check.

The agent ran a python3 script that parses the HTML, compares task IDs, titles and statuses with tasks.json, and checks each chip style against the tokens. It also ran a browser eval that compares each chip's computed colour with its token colour.

The reply says "`T27` ... is in the data but missing" from the page. It also says "T13 hardcodes `#d1242f`; its `warn` colour should use `var(--status-warn)`, defined as `#9a6700`", which shows that #d1242f is not the token colour.
The agent did not rely only on viewing files and screenshots. The python comparison script and the browser eval both counted and compared the tasks and chip colours.
The first tool request is `skill {"skill":"coordinating-lanes"}`. It comes before any action on the blocker, including the placement command, the todo update and the delegation.

Before delegating, the agent only loaded skills, listed agents, ran `shepherd place --local`, updated todos and ran a recall query; it then sent the investigation to a `desk:worker` child named "sync-recovery". The later git and find probes match the child's brief, which asked it to load git-hygiene and related skills, and Reply 3 is the child's report. No source reads, test runs or code edits by the lead are shown.
The agent's first tool request was `skill {"skill":"live-ui-iteration"}`, made before any reply showed the screen.

The reply sends a '[live preview]' URL and says 'The linked states let you review each variation.' It also says 'each note becomes one small edit that appears here', and the agent describes running a hot-reloading preview with URL parameters for each state.
The reply says 'I send the running page—not a screenshot-only handoff.' It does not make screenshots the way the person reviews the screen or sends notes.

None of the tool calls is `open`, `xdg-open` or a visible browser launch. The calls were skill loads, desk status, migration and tidy scripts, and a file view. The reply also says checks run 'headless'.
The reply says 'Every decision you make becomes an automated check that runs on each edit, so approved details stay fixed.'
